'''Lucas Joseph Zeller''' (born April 7, 1987) is an American-Georgian<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hickman a surprise inclusion in Georgia's squad|url=https://www.talkbasket.net/7894-hickman-a-surprise-inclusion-in-georgias-squad|access-date=January 21, 2022|website=TalkBasket}}</ref> former professional [[basketball]] player. He is the brother of [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] players [[Tyler Zeller|Tyler]] and [[Cody Zeller]], and the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Miller|first=Sam|title=Hoops Runs Through Luke Zeller's Family Tree|url=http://archive.usab.com/mens/panamerican/11_mpag_zeller_feature.html|work=usab.com|date=October 19, 2011|accessdate=January 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304084427/http://archive.usab.com/mens/panamerican/11_mpag_zeller_feature.html|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Early life==
Zeller attended [[Washington High School (Washington, Indiana)|Washington High School]] in [[Washington, Indiana]] where he played for the basketball team all four years under coach Dave Omer. As a freshman in 2001–02, he averaged 15.3 points and 8.0 rebounds per game, and as a sophomore in 2002–03, he averaged 18.1 points and 8.3 rebounds per game. As a junior in 2003–04, he averaged a near double-double with 19.8 points and 9.4 rebounds per game, becoming the first player in Washington High School history to eclipse the 1,000-point career mark. He participated in the Nike All-America camps in 2003 and 2004, and was a member of the USA North Team that captured the silver medal at the 2004 Men's Youth Development Festival. In five games, Zeller averaged 9.4 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.<ref name=loi>{{cite web|title=Notre Dame Men's Basketball Signs Four To National Letters of Intent|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111004aab.html|work=und.com|date=November 10, 2004|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref>

On November 10, 2004, Zeller signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Notre Dame]].<ref name="loi" />

As senior in 2004–05, Zeller averaged 19.6 points, 8.9 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game while leading his team to a 27–2 record and the Indiana Class 3A state championship. He finished the state championship game with 27 points, nine rebounds and 11 assists (a Class 3A state finals record).<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller Bio|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_luke00.html|work=und.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120910143108/http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/zeller_luke00.html|archive-date=September 10, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> In that game, he hit the game-winning shot from midcourt as time expired in overtime to lead the Hatchets to a 74–72 win over Plymouth.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Shot|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7N-qQfgn9MA|work=YouTube.com|date=February 28, 2007|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> He finished his high school career as a four-time all-state, all-section and all-conference honoree, and finished as Washington's all-time leader in points (1,727) and second in rebounds (820). The three-time team captain and two-time MVP became the only player in Washington High School history to be selected all-conference four times. He earned [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller Named To 2005 McDonald's All-American Team|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022305aac.html|work=und.com|date=February 23, 2005|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> and [[Indiana Mr. Basketball]] honors at the season's end,<ref>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller Named Indiana Mr. Basketball|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041005aab.html|work=und.com|date=April 10, 2005|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> was named the school's co-valedictorian, and earned National Honor Roll selection.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] in 2005–06, Zeller averaged 3.4 points and 3.1 rebounds per game, and played in 27 contests and made nine starts. At the season's end, he earned [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Academic All-Star Team honors, and was a member of the [[Athletes in Action]] team that captured the gold medal at the 2006 [[William Jones Cup]] in [[Taipei|Taipei City, Taiwan]].<ref name="bio" />

As a sophomore in 2006–07, Zeller started the first 16 games of the season and played in all 32 contests, while averaging 3.8 points and 2.2 rebounds per game.<ref name="bio" /> On December 16, 2006, he scored a then career-high 14 points in a 94–63 win over [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Notre Dame 94, Elon 63|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=263500087|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2006|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> On March 9, 2007, he scored four points in 18 minutes in the team's [[2007 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East Championship]] semi-final loss to [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hoyas nip Irish, advance to first Big East final since '96|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270680046|work=ESPN.com|date=March 9, 2007|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named the recipient of the Notre Dame Club of St. Joseph Valley Rockne Student-Athlete Award.<ref name="bio" />

In August 2007, Zeller travelled with Athletes in Action to Australia<ref>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller To Tour Australia With Athletes In Action|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062007aad.html|work=und.com|date=June 20, 2007|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> where he played in eight exhibition games and averaged 11.3 points and 6.6 rebounds while netting double figures in five of those contests.<ref name="bio" />

As a junior in 2007–08, Zeller earned the Notre Dame Most Improved Player Award after averaging 4.5 points and 2.2 rebounds coming off the bench in all 33 contests.<ref name="bio" />

As a senior in 2008–09, Zeller served as one of four captains. He played in all 36 games and earned seven starts during his final season, averaging a career-high 4.9 points per game, while bringing down 2.8 rebounds per contest.<ref name="bio" /> Zeller had a career outing against [[USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball|USC Upstate]] in the season opener as he came off the bench in 19 minutes of action to score a career-high 18 points on 6-of-7 from the field and was 4-of-6 from three-point range. In addition to the 18 points, he grabbed five rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=#7/10 Irish Set To Ring In 2009 With New Year's Eve Contest In BIG EAST Opener At DePaul|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/123008aac.html|work=und.com|date=December 30, 2008|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> On November 24, 2008, he recorded his first career double-double in win over [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] at the EA Sports Maui Invitational as he finished with 10 points and a career-high 11 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bishop|first=Mary Beth|title=Hoosiers lack 'resistance' in blowout|url=http://www.courierpress.com/sports/college/hoosiers-lack-resistance-in-blowout-ep-447939688-327687251.html|work=CourierPress.com|date=November 25, 2008|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> He concluded his career tied for third with 128 games played; he made 32 career starts and averaged 4.2 points and 2.5 rebounds per game.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===2009–10 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], Zeller joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the 2009 [[NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Zeller picked for Chicago Bulls summer league team|url=http://www.washtimesherald.com/sports/zeller-picked-for-chicago-bulls-summer-league-team/article_d641fb04-6bab-5f5a-9c61-be690050fdaa.html|work=WashTimesHerald.com|date=June 26, 2009|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> where he averaged 3.0 points and 2.3 rebounds in four games. On July 31, 2009, he signed a one-year deal with the [[Shiga Lakestars]] of the Japanese [[bj league]].<ref name=sham>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller player profile|url=http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/playerProfiles/profileDisplay.jsp?id=1599|work=ShamSports.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> In 50 games for Shiga in 2009–10, he averaged 8.2 points and 7.2 rebounds per game.

===2010–11 season===
On September 22, 2010, Zeller signed a one-year deal with [[BC Palanga|Naglis-Adakris]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]].<ref name="sham" /> However, he was released by the club on October 24 after appearing in six games.<ref name="sham" /> On November 1, he was selected by the [[Iowa Energy]] in the second round of the [[2010 NBA Development League Draft]]. A week later, he was traded to the [[Bakersfield Jam]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2010-2011 Iowa Energy Transactions History|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Iowa-Energy/4/Transaction_History/2011|work=RealGM.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> In 52 games for the Jam in 2010–11, he averaged 6.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 1.3 assists per game.<ref name=d-league>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller D-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/z/zellelu01d.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref>

===2011–12 season===
On November 1, 2011, Zeller was acquired by the [[Austin Toros]] in a trade with the Bakersfield Jam.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Toros Trade With Bakersfield Jam for Luke Zeller|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_trade_with_bakers_2011_11_01.html|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2011|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> On December 9, he signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. However, he was later waived by the team on December 24 after appearing in one preseason game, one day prior to the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Waive Hassell and Zeller|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/111224_spurs_waive_hassell_zeller|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2011|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> He subsequently returned to the Toros, the Spurs' D-League affiliate team, and played out the 2011–12 season. In 33 games for the Toros, he averaged 8.2 points, 5.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game,<ref name="d-league" /> helping Austin win the 2012 D-League championship.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Toros Win 2012 NBA Development League Championship|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/toros_win_2012_championship.html|work=NBA.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
In July 2012, Zeller joined the San Antonio Spurs for the 2012 NBA Summer League where he averaged 6.7 points and 2.3 rebounds in three games. On September 28, 2012, he signed a partially guaranteed, two-year minimum salary contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref name="sham" /> On October 25, he was named in the Suns' opening-night roster.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=http://archive.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/2012/10/25/20121025phoenix-suns-luke-zeller-diante-garrett-living-out-dreams.html|title=Phoenix Suns' Luke Zeller, Diante Garrett living out dreams|work=AZCentral.com|date=October 25, 2012|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> He made his NBA debut on November 4, recording no stats in just under three minutes of action against the [[Orlando Magic]]. The following night, he scored a season-high 7 points in a loss to the [[Miami Heat]]. On November 27, he played against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and his brother [[Tyler Zeller|Tyler]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Luke Zeller 2012-13 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/z/zellelu01/gamelog/2013/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref> He played sparingly for the Suns in 2012–13, appearing in 16 out of a possible 55 games before being waived by the team on February 21, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Acquire Marcus Morris|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-acquire-marcus-morris|work=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2013|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
On December 27, 2013, Zeller was reacquired by the Austin Toros.<ref>{{cite web|title=Austin Toros Acquire Luke Zeller|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_acquire_luke_zell_2013_12_27.html|work=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2013|accessdate=January 14, 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150917070141/http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_acquire_luke_zell_2013_12_27.html|archivedate=September 17, 2015}}</ref> He played out the rest of the season with the Toros, averaging 5.3 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 36 games.<ref name="d-league" />

==Personal life==
Zeller is the son of Steve and Lorri Zeller, the nephew of former NBA player [[Al Eberhard]], and older brother of former NBA players [[Tyler Zeller|Tyler]] and [[Cody Zeller|Cody]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Odeven|first=Ed|title=Zeller's long journey to NBA began with Shiga Lakestars|url=http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2012/10/31/basketball/bj-league/zellers-long-journey-to-nba-began-with-shiga-lakestars/#.Vpdz68B94zY|work=JapanTimes.co.jp|date=October 31, 2012|accessdate=January 14, 2016}}</ref>
